### Relevant User Guidance – Functions Using LWLock for Synchronization:

PostgreSQL employs Lightweight Locks (`LWLocks`) internally throughout its architecture, particularly for managing concurrency across various internal operations like buffer pool management, page-level writes, Xact management, etc. Here’s how you can systematically identify all functions relying explicitly on LWLock APIs programmatically:

```sql
SELECT p.oid::regproc AS func_name,
       pg_get_functiondef(p.oid),
       pr.pronamespace || '.' || quote_ident(pr.prname) AS schema_and_function,
       l.lock_type,
       count(*) OVER () AS total_functions_using_lwlocks
FROM pg_proc p JOIN pg_lock_status() ls ON ls.objid = p.oid
JOIN pg_namespace n ON p.pronamespace = n.oid
JOIN pg_class c ON p.prorettype = c.reloid AND c.relkind IN ('r', 't')
WHERE ls.mode LIKE '%Exclusive%'
AND EXISTS (
    SELECT FROM unnest(pg_depend.refobjid) dep WHERE dep.oprcode = 'pg_lwlock'
);
```
